hardhat-promised@2.21.0 was published to npm on 2026-10-06 13:59 UTC by user ryan.danial915 (account's only package, created the same day). The name targets the Ethereum development tool hardhat. The package is a verbatim copy of the pino logger (README, docs, lib/*.js, SECURITY.md; the README badges still point to pino) with one file added that pino does not contain: lib/config.js, a single-line 4,373,384-byte obfuscated script (javascript-obfuscator style, hex-escaped string table, control-flow flattening). index.js requires ./lib/config on line 6, so the payload runs as soon as the package is required; the exported 'middleware' is a no-op. The dependency axios, which pino does not use, was added for the payload. package.json carries a fake author (Robert King <hello@jsonspack.com>) and no repository.

Behavior observed when lib/config.js is loaded in an instrumented sandbox: (1) child_process.spawn of a detached node process (node --max-old-space-size=4096 --no-warnings -, script fed over stdin, stdout and stderr ignored, windowsHide: true, detached: true), i.e. a hidden background process that outlives the parent; (2) code construction through the Function constructor; (3) axios.post of JSON to http://167.88.172.33:8087/api/log containing os.hostname(), os.platform()/release()/type() and os.userInfo().username, with a fixed key ukey=301, a tag t=3, a timestamp and a SHA-256 'validation' header. The messages posted are 'Starting client', 'Spawning autoUploadScript', 'Spawning ldbScript', 'Spawning socketScript' and the matching 'Failed to spawn ...' errors, which name three stealer modules: automatic file upload, LevelDB (browser extension / wallet storage) reading, and a persistent socket connection to the operator.

Trigger: on import (require). Type: trojanized copy of a popular library acting as an information-stealer loader with a hard-coded C2 at 167.88.172.33:8087.
